SELECTION guard (old option 1) still has value — it stops lnrent from ever PICKING a
low-base/high-ppm gateway visible at preflight — but it must not be described as closing the
send-time reprice race. Revise the acceptance criteria accordingly.

title: Buyer cancel/renew during the transient RESUMING state
description:
**RESUMING renew/cancel is P3 UX-ONLY — the money bug CANNOT occur.** The feared cancel/renew-during-RESUMING money-loss path does not exist: order_intake gates cancel and renew to ACTIVE|SUSPENDED (order_intake.rs:317,379,922), so a cancel/renew that lands in the transient RESUMING window is simply DROPPED (Ok(()) + warn) — it never flips state, never bypasses the resume driver, never strands a paid renewal. The money-path audit confirmed this (production-readiness.md "Dispositions for existing open beads", lnrent-z4u: downgrade to a P3 UX residue).

## Residual — the only work here
The buyer gets NO reply DM when they cancel/renew during the transient RESUMING window (usually sub-second; up to minutes on a slow/failing resume hook, 3x120s). RESUMING self-resolves (resume -> ACTIVE, or fail -> SUSPENDED+refund), after which cancel/renew behave normally. This is a small operator/buyer UX polish, not a correctness fix.

## Scope
- Decide and implement ONE of: (a) send an informational "a renewal is being applied — please retry in a moment" reply for a cancel/renew received in RESUMING, or (b) keep the drop and DOCUMENT it as accepted behavior. Note renew has no error-reply variant in wire::Msg, so a renew reply would ride billing.notice or accept the drop — settle that in the design.
- NO state machinery: do NOT add a RESUMING->CANCELLED transition, a pending-cancel queue, resume-driver integration, or any refund/restore path. Those are OUT of scope (they would be a new feature guarding a bug that cannot occur — overengineering, the top project risk).

## Guardrail — preserve, for a FUTURE scope expansion ONLY (not this bead)
If a later effort ever expands scope to make cancel actually FUNCTION during RESUMING: do NOT naively flip RESUMING->CANCELLED — that bypasses the resume driver (which CASes on state='RESUMING'), leaving the renewal neither resumed nor refunded (paid, VM off, no refund; this was a reverted codex-gate P1). The safe design would route the cancel THROUGH the resume driver (record a pending-cancel applied after it resolves, or have the resume path claim RESUMING-origin CANCELLED rows and refund/restore). Recorded so the trap is never re-discovered the hard way — explicitly NOT in scope here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A short design note decides reply-vs-documented-drop for cancel/renew in RESUMING; if a reply is chosen it is a plain informational DM with NO state change.
- No RESUMING->CANCELLED shortcut and no new refund/resume/pending-cancel machinery is introduced (grep/review check).
- Reply path: a unit test that a cancel/renew received while the sub is RESUMING produces the informational reply and leaves sub state unchanged. Documented-drop path: the behavior is documented and a test asserts the drop leaves state unchanged.
- Gates: `cargo test -p lnrentd` green, `clippy` clean.

Related: [[PR-21]] (lnrent-urw.8) — the other RESUMING-window correctness concern (suspend/destroy hook race). This bead is UX-only; PR-21 is the money-core one.
close_reason: Merged as PR #57. Daemon sends a stateless billing.notice for cancel/renew during transient RESUMING (owner-only after auth, no state change — no RESUMING->CANCELLED shortcut). order_intake only, 664 tests. codex P2 (CLI renew doesn't surface the notice — client only awaits request-correlated billing.invoice; BillingNotice has no correlation field) is additive/no-regression and split to follow-up lnrent-zs2 (client-crate: add correlation + surface on renew/cancel), draining next. CodeRabbit trivial test-assertion nit only.

title: clients: surface the RESUMING billing.notice on the buyer renew/cancel path
description:
Follow-up to lnrent-z4u (codex P2 on PR #57). z4u makes the DAEMON send a stateless billing.notice ('a renewal is being applied — please retry in a moment') for a cancel/renew received while the sub is transiently RESUMING. But the BUYER CLIENT never surfaces it on the renew path: clients/core/src/client.rs renew() only matches a request-correlated Msg::BillingInvoice, so exchange() skips the notice and times out — the buyer still sees the OLD timeout, not the new feedback. (The daemon change is strictly additive / no regression: the CLI renew timed out before z4u too.)

## The gap
- Msg::BillingNotice carries NO correlation field ({ state, message }), so the client cannot correlate a notice to a specific renew.request or subscription.
- clients/core renew() returns Result<BillingInvoice, BuyerError> — no way to return a notice outcome.
- cancel path: confirm whether the client cancel flow awaits a reply; if it does, surface the notice there too.

## Scope (option: teach the client to recognize the notice)
1. Add a correlation field to BillingNotice (subscription_id at least; request_id optional) in the wire type; daemon order_intake populates it for the RESUMING notice (it has the sub_id).
2. clients/core renew() (and cancel if it awaits): matcher also accepts an operator billing.notice correlated by subscription_id; return type distinguishes invoice-vs-notice (e.g. an enum RenewReply::Invoice | RenewReply::Retry(message)).
3. clients/cli: display the notice message on the renew/cancel command instead of a timeout error.
4. Keep it additive — no state change, owner-only semantics unchanged.

## Acceptance
- A buyer running the CLI/web renew (and cancel, if it awaits) against a RESUMING sub sees the 'retry in a moment' notice instead of a timeout.
- BillingNotice correlation added; daemon populates it; no regression to the normal billing.invoice / cancel-ack paths.
- Tests: clients/core renew() against a RESUMING sub returns the notice outcome (not a timeout); gates green (clippy + workspace tests).
close_reason: Merged as PR #58. request_id-correlate the RESUMING renew billing.notice: wire BillingNotice + optional request_id, daemon handle_renew echoes req.id, clients/core renew() accepts a request-correlated RESUMING notice immediately -> RenewReply::Retry (stale relay replay w/ different id ignored; no timeout wait), Msg::request_id()/dedupe_id() expose it, CLI+web tag retry. Finished BY HAND after rb-lite consensus_failure (my task's no-request_id non-goal blocked the fix); addressed 2 codex P2 rounds (client gap, wire helper). Gates green (clippy 0, 671 tests + wire+renew tests); CI green incl. web e2e.

title: Supervisor catch-up must honor a live settled_at (caps a late LIVE payment -> wrong provision)
description:
## Problem (codex P1; gated behind fedimint-off but also latent on the mock path)
supervisor.rs settlement_catch_up (boot + maintenance loop) scans OPEN store invoices and for any the backend reports lookup()==Paid FABRICATES a CAPPED recovered_settled_at (supervisor.rs:~1033/1049: capped < expires_at for an order). Correct for a RECOVERY settlement (settled-while-down, true time unknown) but WRONG for a LIVE settlement whose true settled_at is known: a late LIVE payment that should REFUND (capture g5p gate at capture.rs:180 refunds at settled_at>=expires_at) can be grabbed by catch-up first -> stamped expires_at-1 -> PROVISIONED. capture is idempotent on external_id so whoever captures first wins -> non-deterministic.

## Fix (design corrected by the codex next-steps review 2026-06-29)
catch-up must use the backend's REAL observed settled_at when known, and CAP only on recovery provenance (true time unknown).
- TRAIT: make lookup() richer OR add `lookup_settlement(id) -> {status, settled_at: Option<i64>}`. catch-up uses Some(real) EXACTLY and caps only on None.
- FedimintPayment: ALREADY persists settled_at in its index (fedimint_backend.rs:74/720) but its lookup() DISCARDS it (fedimint_backend.rs:357) — surface it.
- MockPayment: does NOT currently store settlement time — it keeps only `paid: HashSet<String>` and DROPS settled_at from settle() (backends.rs:187/219). CHANGE the mock to store external_id->settled_at (a live mock settle records the real ts; a recovery has None). [the earlier bead wrongly said the mock already stored it]
- capture: NO policy change needed (g5p gate already keys off the real Settlement.settled_at).
- TEST: a regression proving a LATE live-paid order REFUNDS (real ts >= expiry) while a RECOVERED/NULL paid order still uses the conservative cap (provisions).

## Notes
Latent on mock today (the .15 e2e tests are deterministic) but a real production race; fix BEFORE enabling fedimint (it is o6p's only graph blocker besides the resolver, now done). Files: supervisor.rs, backends.rs (trait + MockPayment), fedimint_backend.rs (lookup), a new catch-up test.
close_reason: DONE + merged (master 490c4ac). Supervisor settlement_catch_up now honors a LIVE settled_at: added PaymentBackend::lookup_settlement(id)->(PaymentStatus, Option<i64>); catch-up uses Some(real) exactly + caps (recovered_settled_at) only on None. MockPayment stores external_id->settled_at + settle_recovered() models recovery; FedimintPayment::lookup_settlement reads its index settled_at (Some=live Claimed, NULL=cached/recovery); lookup() unchanged (reconcile untouched); NO capture policy change. Regression settlement_catch_up_refunds_late_live_order_but_caps_recovery + existing recovery scenarios switched to settle_recovered (cap preserved). Built via watched rb-lite — converged CLEAN in 1 codex+claude round; cargo test + clippy (default + --features fedimint) green.

title: Listing publishes unconditionally on boot: no publish gate, no withdraw verb, WITHDRAWN is dead schema
description:
Found by the 2026-07-26 codex+fable status analysis. codex independently named this the
single biggest risk the project carries: "uncontrolled production exposure ... converts every
unresolved P1 into immediate, attacker-scalable financial liability."

## The defect
On start the listing row is born `'ACTIVE'` (daemon/src/supervisor.rs:317-324) and published
immediately (supervisor.rs:352-363, called unconditionally from `start` at supervisor.rs:490).
docs/go-live.md:30-33 already admits orders are possible "already during the preflight checks."

The only state that suppresses publication, `'WITHDRAWN'`, is NEVER WRITTEN BY ANY CODE PATH.
It exists solely as a schema comment (daemon/src/store.rs:256) and a no-resurrect guard
(supervisor.rs:317-320). There is no CLI or IPC verb to withdraw, pause, or unpublish a listing
— not at launch, not ever. An operator who needs to stop taking orders (maintenance, capacity
exhausted, a bad recipe, an incident) has no affordance short of killing the daemon.

## Why this blocks lnrent-2em
2em's acceptance says "go-live.md reordered so preflight precedes publication". THAT CANNOT BE
DONE BY EDITING THE DOC — there is no gate to reorder. lnrent-1sr built the recipe preflight to
catch broken provisioning params BEFORE payment; publishing before preflight runs defeats it.
This is a code bead hiding inside a drill bead's doc-sounding acceptance criterion, and it must
drain BEFORE 2em runs or the drill stalls at exactly that step.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The daemon can start WITHOUT publishing, so an operator can run `lnrent preflight` against a
  live daemon before any buyer can order. Whether that is an explicit publish opt-in or
  publication gated on a passing preflight is the implementer's call; the required outcome is
  that preflight can precede public exposure.
- A real `WITHDRAWN` transition exists and is reachable: an operator verb (CLI/IPC) that
  withdraws a published listing, and one that (re)publishes it. The existing no-resurrect guard
  (supervisor.rs:317-320) must keep holding — a withdrawn listing must not return on next boot.
- docs/go-live.md reordered so preflight precedes publication, and the "starting the daemon IS
  the go-live" framing corrected to match.
- Tests: boot-without-publish; withdraw then restart does not republish; publish after a passing
  preflight; a failing preflight does not publish.
close_reason:
Closed by PR #70 (squash 4a99098). All acceptance criteria met.

- A fresh daemon takes NO orders until the operator publishes: the boot upsert creates the row
  UNPUBLISHED and never writes ACTIVE, and its ON CONFLICT clause omits `state` so a WITHDRAWN
  listing is never resurrected.
- Publication is an explicit act (`lnrent listing publish`), one-time rather than per-boot — the
  durable row is the authority, so later boots republish with no operator action.
- `lnrent listing withdraw` exists, is the only writer of WITHDRAWN, persists across restarts, and
  retracts from the relays best-effort (a relay failure is a diagnostic, never a reason to reverse
  the durable withdrawal).
- Publish gates on preflight, split by failure class: STRUCTURAL hard-blocks with no override,
  REACHABILITY warns and is overridable with `--accept-unverified`.
- Nothing auto-withdraws a live listing.
- `lnrent status` reports whether the listing is published.
- docs/go-live.md reordered so preflight precedes publication.

This unblocks lnrent-2em, whose acceptance ("go-live.md reordered so preflight precedes
publication") was literally unimplementable before: there was no gate to reorder.

## Review record
The branch went through an 11-pass codex + Claude Fable review loop AFTER a 6-round rb-lite run and
a codex PR-bot round. That loop found 18 further defects, including three P1s in the publish/withdraw
path: an in-flight order could outrun `listing withdraw` and commit a payable invoice after the
operator's stop; an order could commit behind a RELEASED capacity hold and let a slot be handed out
twice; and a crash between the hold release and the refusal cache left a request that could never be
answered, because `reservation::reserve` bails on a terminal row.

Six of the eighteen were false or stale JUSTIFICATIONS rather than broken logic — most seriously
operator-facing text asserting "the money path fails closed at order time", which holds for the
payment backend and NOT for the compute provider (`order_intake` never consults it), so overriding a
provider outage costs a Buyer their refund fees. Six more were defects introduced by earlier fixes
within the loop itself, including a comment falsified by a later commit in the same loop.

## Residual, shipped knowingly
lnrent-yxg (same-second relist after a restart) remains open and is disclosed in the code comment.
All three independent reviewers converged on it as the sole outstanding item, and the PR bot's final
pass improved its recorded fix: the durable timestamp must be stamped wherever the NIP-09 deletion is
SENT, not on the state transition, or the `AlreadyWithdrawn` re-retraction is missed.

the NIP-99 `30402` event ALREADY SITTING ON RELAYS. Without that, a "withdrawn" listing stays
discoverable: buyers still find it and their orders bounce at intake
(`daemon/src/order_intake.rs:144-158` rejects a non-ACTIVE listing), which is money-safe but reads to
the buyer as a broken operator.

Add: withdrawing a listing also retracts it from the relays best-effort — delete/expire the 30402
event, or republish it in a withdrawn form. Best-effort is the right bar: relays may be unreachable
and the durable row remains the authority, so a failed retraction must not block or reverse the local
withdrawal.

Also worth deciding IN THE TASK FILE before rb-lite runs, rather than leaving it to the reviewer
panel: whether publication becomes an explicit opt-in, or is gated on a passing `lnrent preflight`.
Both satisfy the outcome (preflight can precede public exposure); they differ in operator ergonomics,
and a panel will churn on it.

title: No released artifact: packaging is PLANNED, so a cold operator cannot complete install
description:
Found by the 2026-07-26 codex+fable status analysis (fable: "2em is scheduled to discover that
on-camera").

## The gap
SPEC.md:1364-1371 marks every distribution path as not-in-tree: `skills/` "PLANNED, not in the
tree yet", `nix/` "flake + NixOS module — PLANNED (today: devshell in flake.nix only)",
`packaging/debian/` "systemd unit + install script — PLANNED". docs/go-live.md §2 tells the
operator to `nix develop . --command cargo build --release` — that is a DEVELOPER path, not an
install.

CONTEXT.md's thesis is an ecosystem of third-party operators, so "clone the repo and have Nix"
IS the onboarding surface. It is the first thing a stranger hits and the last thing the graph
owns.

## Why it is filed now instead of during the drill
lnrent-2em's drill step 1 is "install a RELEASED artifact (not a dev build)", and its acceptance
defers gaps found mid-drill to new beads. But this gap is already known with certainty: a cold
operator cannot take step one. Discovering it on-camera wastes the drill, so pre-file it and
drain it first.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A versioned, downloadable release artifact exists for at least one target. A portable
  `lnrentd` + `lnrent` + `lnrent-buyer` binary set is the minimum bar; the NixOS module and
  debian packaging may remain PLANNED.
- A systemd unit ships with it, matching go-live.md's durability guidance (`Restart=always`,
  SIGTERM drain) AND its seed-delivery hygiene (§3: `LoadCredential=` or stdin — never the run
  environment, which go-live.md:89-99 explicitly forbids).
- An install doc that goes from "fresh Debian/NixOS VPS" to "lnrentd running" with NO repo clone
  and NO Rust toolchain.
- SPEC.md §14 updated to describe what actually ships.
- Verified by installing on a clean VPS from the published artifact alone.

title: No alert when a buyer PAID but the settlement cannot be booked (fee-credit refusal / index divergence)
description:
Found by the 2026-07-26 codex+fable status analysis.

## The gap
`AlertKind` (daemon/src/alerts.rs:86-105) covers RefundParked, RefundStuck, TeardownFailed,
RelayBlackout, HoldingsLow, PaidServiceDestroyed, SweepFailed, SweepStuck. NOTHING fires when a
settlement the backend has ALREADY observed as PAID cannot be booked by lnrent. The buyer's
money is gone, the order does not progress, and the operator's phone stays silent.

## Two live paths reach this state
(a) FEE-CREDIT REFUSAL — `spendable_credit_msat` bails (daemon/src/phoenixd_backend.rs:600-623)
    when the wallet-level fee credit could account for the receipt in FULL (lnrent-xk3's
    ADR-0019 reject form: phoenixd exposes no per-receipt attribution, so the refusal is
    wallet-level — see lnrent-itw). Capture never runs; the invoice sits Paid-at-backend /
    OPEN-locally until the operator funds the wallet. Today this is `tracing::error!` only.
    THIS IS NOT EXOTIC: it is the EXPECTED state of an unfunded phoenixd operator's first small
    sale — the same first-receive economics lnrent-ohd documents (25,000 sat in, 2,723 credited).
(b) INDEX DIVERGENCE — the fail-closed arm at phoenixd_backend.rs:1429-1448 after a bad restore:
    a settlement whose index row is missing refuses rather than guessing.

## What is and is not wrong here
Both paths are correctly FAIL-CLOSED — the money-safety behaviour is right and must not change.
What is missing is the OPERATOR SURFACE: the condition is durable, needs a human, and has no
notification. lnrent-7di added exactly this shape for a livelocked sweep (SweepStuck); this is
its mirror on the RECEIVE side.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A durable operator DM alert fires when a backend-PAID settlement has failed to book for longer
  than a threshold, carrying which reason (fee-credit refusal vs index divergence) and its remedy.
- Additive to `AlertKind`, edge-triggered on the existing per-condition cooldown (mirror
  RefundStuck / SweepStuck), riding the durable outbox.
- Surfaced in `lnrent money` / `lnrent status` so an operator who does not read DMs still sees it.
- Tests for both trigger paths plus the cooldown.
- NO money logic changes: this is REPORTING of an already-correct refusal.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Acceptance addition (2026-07-28 codex+fable status analysis): the refusal CASCADES into suspending a
buyer who paid.

This bead currently covers the missing ALERT. It does not name the deadline interaction, which is
what turns a silent condition into lost service:

A RENEWAL settlement refused by `spendable_credit_msat` never reaches capture, so `paid_through`
never advances. `fire_suspend` (`daemon/src/reconcile.rs:251-267`) then fires on the cursor with no
knowledge that a backend-`Paid`-but-unbookable settlement is sitting there — so the buyer PAID and
gets suspended, then destroyed after retention. Money is eventually safe (capture's
terminal-settlement gate refunds net-of-fees), but the service is gone and the operator's reputation
with it.

Per this bead's own framing, that is NOT exotic: it is the expected state of an unfunded first-time
phoenixd operator, whose first small sale can land entirely in fee credit (measured 2026-07-26).

Add to acceptance:
- The alert threshold must be required to fire WELL BEFORE `effective_suspend_at`, so the operator
  has a real window to fund the wallet before a paying buyer is suspended. State the relationship
  explicitly rather than picking an arbitrary timeout.
- The cascade itself (refused renewal -> paid_through frozen -> fire_suspend -> destroy) is named in
  the bead and covered by a test, so the alert is justified by the harm it prevents rather than by
  "an error was logged".

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Unrecorded DECISION, flagged by the 2026-07-29 codex+fable analysis. Settle it in the task file
before this drains, or the implementer picks silently.

The earlier comment established the cascade: a renewal settlement refused by `spendable_credit_msat`
never reaches capture, so `paid_through` never advances, and `fire_suspend`
(daemon/src/reconcile.rs:251-267) then suspends — and after retention destroys — a Buyer who PAID.
The remedy recorded was "the alert must fire WELL BEFORE `effective_suspend_at`".

That remedy is alert-only: it relies on an operator reading a DM in time. Nobody has decided whether
reconcile should instead HOLD the suspend while a backend-PAID-but-unbookable settlement exists for
that subscription.

Both answers are defensible:
- ALERT-ONLY: avoids a new coupling between reconcile's deadline scan and backend settlement state,
  keeps the money path's authority in the ledger (ADR-0016), and the operator has a real window.
- HOLD: an unfunded first-time phoenixd operator is exactly who hits this (their first small sale can
  land entirely in fee credit — measured 2026-07-26), and that operator is also the least likely to
  be watching DMs. Suspending a paying Buyer is a service-loss the alert only mitigates if someone
  is awake.

Whichever is chosen, record the reasoning in the code where the suspend decision is made, not only
in the bead — this project has repeatedly lost the "why" and re-derived it wrongly.

title: Operator docs assert two false things: GATE-0 'not landed' + a dangling ADR-0018 spec pointer
description:
Found by the 2026-07-26 codex+fable status analysis. Two normative operator-facing statements
that are verifiably wrong against the tree. Both are roughly one-line fixes and share one pass.

## (1) go-live.md tells operators GATE-0 has not landed. It landed 2026-07-08.
docs/go-live.md:32-35 says: "Until the GATE-0 abuse-resistance items in
`docs/specs/production-readiness.md` land (per-buyer reservation caps, inbound rate-limiting), a
stranger can hold your capacity at zero cost, so an attended launch accepts that documented risk
knowingly."

They landed. The `lnrent-gdu` epic and all four children are CLOSED (2026-07-08): gdu.1
per-pubkey cap on outstanding live HELD reservations, gdu.2 per-pubkey inbound token bucket in
`process_inbound`, gdu.3 authorize the op.request reject path before the durable claim, gdu.4
cap unpaid invoice load + params size + engine message size. The per-buyer cap is live at
daemon/src/reservation.rs:100 and reservation.rs:137, with five tests at reservation.rs:771-849.

The runbook makes a stranger operator knowingly accept a risk that was closed 18 days before
this bead was filed — and lnrent-2em's drill subject reads this file FIRST.

## (2) ADR-0018 points at a spec file that does not exist.
docs/adr/0018-payment-backends-lnv2-phoenixd-retire-lnv1.md:66 sends the reader to
`docs/specs/backend-strategy.md` for "the execution detail". That file is not in the tree
(lnrent-bi8 closed superseded). A dangling normative pointer in a live ADR.

lnrent-ehu criterion 5 ("backend-neutral operator documentation verified against reality") would
eventually catch both — but ehu closes LAST, after the very drill that reads these files.

- go-live.md accurately states what GATE-0 shipped and what abuse surface, if any, genuinely
  remains. The "attended launch" rationale is re-derived from what is ACTUALLY still open, not
  from the stale list.
- ADR-0018:66 either points at a file that exists or states inline where the execution detail
  now lives.
- A sweep confirming no other operator-facing doc names closed work as pending.

title: phoenixd_invoice index GC is deferred to a bead that was never filed
description:
Found by the 2026-07-26 codex+fable status analysis.

## Why this bead exists at all
daemon/src/phoenixd_backend.rs:132-139 defers index GC in the module header, naming the
PRECEDENT beads (lnrent-y4m.15 / lnrent-y4m.19 — both closed, both lnv2-only) but no OWNING
bead, and none existed in the graph. Every other deferral in that same header (lnrent-kr1,
lnrent-itw, lnrent-tof) IS a real filed bead, and the header claims "all filed, none silently
dropped". This one was the exception. Same for the websocket-listener "TODO (follow-up bead)"
at phoenixd_backend.rs:126.

## What it is
`phoenixd_invoice` grows one row per created invoice — the same unpaid-order flood surface lnv2
grew a throttled reaper for. The header is honest that this is an OPERATIONAL bound (disk), not
money-safety: the poll reads only rows whose bolt11 can still be paid (an indexed `expires_at`
range, not a table scan) and retires within that set, so steady-state poll cost tracks LIVE
invoices rather than table size. No row here is authoritative over money — phoenixd is.

## The trap that must be ported, not re-derived
The lookup fail-closed arm (phoenixd_backend.rs:1429-1448) leaves the future reaper a
LOAD-BEARING instruction: a reaper that deletes a row which is still lookup-able turns
fail-closed into a permanent retry. lnv2's equivalent money-safety rules are already worked out
— y4m.19 reaps FAILED-only and deliberately KEEPS SUCCEEDED, and left `fedimint_pay_dead_op`
un-GC'd because reaping it reintroduces a double-refund brick. File this now so that reasoning
does not decay along with the module context.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Throttled, chunked reaper for terminal `phoenixd_invoice` rows, mirroring y4m.15/y4m.19's
  money-safety split rather than inventing a new policy.
- Provably cannot reap a row the fail-closed lookup arm (phoenixd_backend.rs:1429-1448) still
  depends on — with a test that pins that interaction.
- The websocket-listener TODO (phoenixd_backend.rs:126) is either folded in here or filed
  separately, so the module header carries no unowned TODO.

title: Seed-only restore rotates phoenixd's api password, so lnrent cannot reach the node after a successful recovery
description:
Found by the lnrent-kr1 seed-only restore drill, run live on the mainnet staging node 2026-07-27.

## What the drill proved, and what it exposed
The drill passed on the money: the data dir was wiped to `seed.dat` alone, and phoenixd rebuilt the
SAME channel (same channelId, same fundingTxId, `state: Normal`) with the balance intact and provably
spendable. ADR-0018's premise holds — the seed is sufficient for the FUNDS.

It is not sufficient for ACCESS. `phoenix.conf` lives inside the wiped data dir, so phoenixd
REGENERATED both api passwords on restart (verified: the new `http-password` differs from the
backed-up one). **`seed.dat` restores MONEY; `phoenix.conf` restores ACCESS**, and only one of them
is what operators are told to back up.

## The failure an operator actually hits
After a successful restore the operator sees their funds back — and lnrent cannot talk to the node,
because the configured `phoenixd_api_password` is now wrong. Every authenticated call fails, so:
- `lnrent preflight` reports `PhoenixdProbe::AuthRejected` (lnrent-5mi) — the RIGHT diagnostic, but
  its remedy text says nothing about a restore having rotated the password, so the operator is left
  suspecting a config typo or a wrong URL.
- the money path fails closed on `backend_ready()` and refund readiness reports the node as down
  (lnrent-p2e's phoenixd vocabulary).
The daemon is behaving correctly; the operator has no way to know WHY from the surfaces provided.

This is squarely CONTEXT.md's product surface: the operator is a stranger, and this fires at the
worst possible moment — mid-recovery, when they are already stressed and reasoning about lost money.

## What to change
1. **docs/go-live.md** (and the phoenixd runbook lnrent-tof will replace it with): the phoenixd
   backup obligation must cover **`phoenix.conf` as well as `seed.dat`**, stating plainly that the
   seed restores the wallet and the conf restores API access. Add the restore-path step: if the conf
   was NOT backed up, read the regenerated password out of the restored node and update lnrent's
   `phoenixd_api_password` before restarting the daemon.
2. **The `AuthRejected` remedy text** (`daemon/src/preflight.rs`, the phoenixd check): name the
   post-restore rotation as a cause alongside a mistyped/rotated password — one clause, not a new
   check. Keep it in step with the money-path wording (lnrent-p2e keeps those two surfaces in
   agreement by construction, so change it in the one probe→text function).
3. Cross-reference from **lnrent-kr1**'s deliverable: whatever the `lnrent phoenixd-seed` helper's
   docs say about backup must not imply the seed alone is a complete backup.

## Non-goals
- Do NOT make lnrent read, manage, or rotate phoenixd's api password. That is the operator's
  credential for an external service they run.
- Do NOT add a new probe, alert kind, or config field. `AuthRejected` already detects this; what is
  missing is only that its remedy names the cause.
- Do NOT change readiness detection or any money logic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- go-live.md's phoenixd section tells the operator to back up `phoenix.conf` alongside `seed.dat`,
  says which artifact restores what, and gives the post-restore step when the conf is missing.
- The `AuthRejected` operator text names a post-restore password regeneration as a possible cause.
- A test pins that wording, in the same style as the existing phoenixd remedy tests.
- lnrent-kr1's backup guidance does not contradict it.

title: Wire the measured completedAt discriminator into phoenixd pay recovery (ends the failed-refund livelock)
description:
Found by the 2026-07-28 codex+fable status analysis. This bead exists because the measurement that
unblocks it was recorded ONLY as a comment on lnrent-tof — a human live-acceptance drill, not a code
bead. That is precisely how lnrent-rpa's gap happened, repeating within 48h of rpa being filed to
correct it.

## The measurement (live, 2026-07-26, phoenixd 0.9.0-b072567)
`completedAt` is the TERMINAL MARKER on an outgoing payment. All three legs observed on real records:

| isPaid | completedAt | meaning   | samples |
|--------|-------------|-----------|---------|
| true   | SET         | SUCCEEDED | 2       |
| false  | SET         | FAILED    | 2       |
| false  | ABSENT      | PENDING   | 1       |

The PENDING leg is a CONTROLLED comparison, not a separate payment: the same `paymentId`
(3d9d75f9-6940-45f6-b611-575a21a91ef9) read twice during one payment, byte-identical except the
in-flight read has no `completedAt` field at all and the terminated read has
`completedAt: 1785101384178`. Captured with `lncli addholdinvoice` + a 50ms poll (an ACINQ
trampoline fails a held HTLC back in ~1.6s), and it cost 0 sat.

## Why it matters operationally
Today EVERY genuinely failed phoenixd refund — a route/liquidity failure after the POST, the common
real-world failure against arbitrary buyer destinations — lands in the "unpaid record, stay Pending"
arm (`daemon/src/phoenixd_backend.rs:936-942`, and the receipt-less arm at `:1147-1157`) and can only
exit via a `RefundStuck` operator DM. Money-safe, but operator-intervention-per-failed-refund is the
current phoenixd design and is its top operational defect. lnrent-tof's acceptance exercises refund
SUCCESS ("failed-provision refund through BOTH an LN-address and an LNURL"); the livelock only shows
on refund FAILURE, so tof would not surface it.

## The stale comment — fix this even if the rest is deferred
`daemon/src/phoenixd_backend.rs:922-942` still states "phoenixd's failed-payment record shape is not
yet measured, so this can be neither confirmed nor refuted here". That is FALSE as of 2026-07-26.
This module's stated doctrine is that its header and comments are the source of truth, so the next
agent to touch the file will trust a stale claim and re-derive a solved question.

## What to build
1. Carry `completedAt` through: `PhoenixdOutgoing` (`:339-344`) has no such field and the wire
   decoder `OutgoingResponse` (`:2288-2299`) DISCARDS it. Both need it (millis, `Option<i64>`,
   `#[serde(default)]` so an absent field decodes as `None` — that absence IS the PENDING signal and
   must never become a decode error).
2. In the `STATUS_PREPARED` recovery arm (`:918-952`), resolve an unpaid record with `completedAt`
   SET to FAILED. Mirror it in the receipt-less arm (`:1147-1157`).
3. **VERSION-BIND IT.** This is OBSERVED behavior of 0.9.0-b072567, not a documented API contract.
   Gate the resolution on the running release matching the verified one (reuse the existing
   `FeeSchedule.verified_version` machinery, `:195-259`); on a version mismatch fall back to today's
   stay-Pending behavior so a phoenixd upgrade re-opens the question instead of silently inheriting
   an assumption about someone else's release.
4. `completedAt` ABSENT must stay Pending FOREVER (lnrent-y4m.16's ambiguous-pay discipline). The
   cost of getting this backwards is a DOUBLE PAY, which is why 3 is mandatory rather than nice.
5. Replace the stale comment at `:922-942` with the measured truth table + the version bind.
6. While here (one-line, same file): the `UnattributedButPayable` warn text (`:601-603`) and enum doc
   (`:503-506`) claim "the spendable balance covers it, so a refund of it can still be paid" — FALSE
   in the partial-credit sub-case. `credit_backing(1000, 999, 0)` classifies `UnattributedButPayable`
   (999 < 1000, so the credit cannot account for the receipt in full) while the balance covers
   nothing. The RULE is right per ADR-0019; only the stated justification is wrong.

## Consequence
This makes `failed_refund_can_reuse_invoice`'s retry apply to REAL payment failures rather than only
the preflight refusals, ending the every-failed-refund-needs-a-DM regime.

## Non-goals
- Do NOT change the refund retry/generation policy itself, the INV-1 cap, or any booking rule.
- Do NOT infer terminality from the HTTP status: `payinvoice` returns HTTP 200 even on FAILURE, with
  a `reason` field and no preimage.
- Do NOT add an alert; `RefundStuck` already exists for what remains genuinely ambiguous.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `completedAt` decoded and carried; absent decodes as `None`, never an error.
- Unpaid + `completedAt` SET resolves FAILED on a version match; unpaid + ABSENT stays Pending; a
  version mismatch falls back to stay-Pending. All three pinned by tests against the measured shapes.
- The stale "not yet measured" comment is gone and the `UnattributedButPayable` text is true.
- Gates green; must compile with and without `--no-default-features`.

title: INV-1 overrun on phoenixd is detected but only logged, and its 'stop automated refunds' remedy stops nothing
description:
Found by the 2026-07-28 codex+fable status analysis.

## The gap
`log_inv1_overrun` (`daemon/src/phoenixd_backend.rs:1250-1261`) detects that a refund COST MORE THAN
THE RECEIPT IT REFUNDS — the exact drain vector ADR-0019 exists to close — and its entire response is
a `tracing::error!` line. Worse, that line instructs "stop automated refunds and reconcile" while
NOTHING actually stops them: the next refund drives straight through the same path.

There is no `AlertKind` for it (`daemon/src/alerts.rs:86-105` covers RefundParked/Stuck,
TeardownFailed, RelayBlackout, HoldingsLow, PaidServiceDestroyed, SweepFailed/Stuck — nothing on the
send side for a cap overrun), so an operator who is not tailing logs learns nothing while each refund
bleeds.

## Why it is reachable
The version gate accepts build-suffixed releases (pinned by the existing test
`the_probe_accepts_the_build_suffixed_version…`), so a custom `0.9.0-bXXXX` whose trampoline fee
schedule differs from the verified one passes preflight and every readiness check. The INV-1
preflight then reserves a fee from the CONFIGURED schedule while the node charges the real one; each
automated refund overruns, and the only trace is a log line.

This is the mirror image of lnrent-gc7 on the receive side, and gc7's argument applies verbatim: the
condition is durable, needs a human, and has no notification.

## What to build
- A durable operator alert when an INV-1 overrun is observed, carrying the excess and the remedy
  (verify the running release and configure `[phoenixd] fee_schedule_*` for it — mirror the wording
  lnrent-5mi's preflight and lnrent-p2e's readiness reporting already use, so the surfaces agree).
- Make the stated remedy TRUE: after an overrun, automated refunds must actually stop (latch a
  refuse-new-automated-refunds flag until the operator clears it) rather than continuing to bleed.
  Follow lnrent-y4m.3's precedent: a latching degraded flag that refuses the dangerous operation
  while leaving reads working, not a panic.
- Existing in-flight/re-awaited refunds must NOT be re-driven into a second pay by the latch —
  y4m.16's discipline still governs; the latch refuses NEW automated attempts only.

## Non-goals
- Do NOT change the INV-1 cap arithmetic or the fee-schedule machinery.
- Do NOT block manual `lnrent refund-retry` — the operator overriding deliberately is the escape
  hatch, and parking every liability with no manual path would strand buyer money.
- Do NOT add a new probe or config field; the detection already exists.

## Acceptance Criteria
- An INV-1 overrun raises a durable, cooldown-keyed operator DM naming the excess and the remedy.
- After an overrun, a NEW automated refund is refused with a specific reason until cleared; a
  re-awaited in-flight refund is unaffected.
- Surfaced in `lnrent money` / `lnrent status` so it is visible without reading DMs.
- Tests for the alert, the latch, the in-flight exemption, and that the manual retry path still works.

title: A relist after a restart can skip the same-second deletion wait, leaving the row ACTIVE behind a rejected 30402
description:
Raised independently by two reviewers: the rb-lite panel (five times, on the lnrent-i23 branch) and
the codex PR bot (P2 on PR #70). Carved out of i23 rather than rushed into an already-large PR.

## The defect
`NostrEngine::wait_out_own_listing_deletion` (`daemon/src/nostr_engine.rs:340`) stops a relist
landing in the SAME Unix second as the NIP-09 retraction that removed it — relays reject a `30402`
published in the same second as its deletion. It reads `last_listing_deletion`, an
`AtomicU64` in PROCESS memory (`nostr_engine.rs:198`), initialized to 0.

So the guard does not survive a restart. Sequence: `listing withdraw` retracts and records the
second in memory only -> the daemon restarts -> the operator republishes within that same second ->
the new engine has 0, skips the wait, and broadcasts. The relay rejects the event, but
`publish_gated` has ALREADY committed the row `ACTIVE`, so `lnrent status` and order intake both
report live while no relay serves the listing. Nothing republishes until the next boot.

## Why the original rejection was too confident
The rejection reasoning was that crossing the window needs a restart PLUS a full publish preflight
(guardian round-trip, TLS provider call, `run_hook` spawn) to complete inside one second, behind the
restart's own join/connect/bind costs. That holds for an interactive operator on a provider-backed
recipe. It does NOT obviously hold for a provider-free recipe with `--accept-unverified`, where
preflight short-circuits nearly everything — which is exactly the shape `clients/web/e2e/run.sh`
runs — under a supervisor restarting automatically. Two independent reviewers landing on it is
itself evidence the window is not as unreachable as claimed.

## The cheap fix — the timestamp is ALREADY durable
Neither reviewer's suggested remedy (a new persisted field, or an unconditional delay) is needed.
`set_state` (`daemon/src/listing.rs`) stamps `updated_at = clock.now()` on every transition,
including the one that writes `WITHDRAWN`. **The withdrawal second is already in the `listing` row.**
The guard just never reads it.

Two things to get right:
1. `upsert_row` OVERWRITES `updated_at` (`ON CONFLICT ... updated_at=excluded.updated_at`), and
   `publish_gated` calls it before the broadcast — so the withdrawal timestamp must be read BEFORE
   that upsert, not after.
2. Put the wait at the RELAY layer, not in the gate. A naive `sleep` inside `publish_gated` would
   fire against a `TestClock` (`set_state` writes `now`, publish then sees `now <= updated_at`) and
   add a real second to every test that publishes. Seeding the engine's existing
   `last_listing_deletion` from the durable row — or passing the retraction second through the
   `ListingRelay` seam — keeps the wait where the real relay is and leaves fakes untouched.

Bound it with the existing `MAX_DELETION_SETTLE_WAIT` so a backwards clock jump cannot hang the
operator's command, exactly as the in-memory path already does.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A withdraw -> restart -> publish sequence inside one second does not produce an `ACTIVE` row whose
  `30402` the relay rejected; either the relist waits the second out, or it does not commit `ACTIVE`.
- The wait derives from the DURABLE withdrawal time, so it survives a restart.
- No test gains a real-time sleep (the `TestClock` paths must not wait).
- The `MAX_DELETION_SETTLE_WAIT` ceiling still applies.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
Refinement to the recorded fix, from the codex PR bot's fresh review of PR #70 (commit 69c40e6).

The bead says to read the withdrawal second from the durable `listing.updated_at`. That is right for
the common path but INCOMPLETE, and the gap is easy to miss: the durable timestamp must cover
"deletion attempts that do not change the listing state" too.

`withdraw` on an already-`WITHDRAWN` row takes the `AlreadyWithdrawn` branch, which DOES re-ask the
relays (that re-retraction is the operator's only affordance for a retraction that never landed) but
writes NOTHING durable — no `set_state`, so no `updated_at` bump. A fix keyed solely on
`listing.updated_at` would therefore miss exactly that retraction, and a relist inside its second
would skip the wait for the same reason the in-memory version does today.

So the durable record has to be written by the RETRACTION, not by the state transition. Options for
the implementer, in rough order of preference:
1. Stamp a dedicated column (or reuse `updated_at`) on EVERY retraction attempt, including the
   already-`WITHDRAWN` branch — the write is what the guard reads, so it must happen wherever the
   NIP-09 deletion is sent.
2. Failing that, treat an unknown/absent timestamp conservatively (wait the full settle window on
   the first relist after a boot) rather than assuming zero means "no recent deletion".

Whichever way, the acceptance criterion "the wait derives from the DURABLE withdrawal time" should
be read as the durable time of the last RETRACTION SENT, not of the last state change.

title: listing withdraw does not void in-flight unpaid orders, but go-live says it stops orders 'immediately'
description:
Found by the 2026-07-29 codex+fable status analysis, in text shipped by lnrent-i23 itself.

## The claim, and why it is not quite true
docs/go-live.md's Stopping section says `lnrent listing withdraw` "marks the listing withdrawn —
which is what actually stops orders, immediately". That is true of NEW orders: order intake refuses
a non-ACTIVE listing, and lnrent-i23 additionally re-checks the listing INSIDE the commit
transaction so an order that was mid-`create_invoice` is refused too.

It is NOT true of orders that already committed. A committed order leaves a PENDING subscription and
an OPEN invoice that stays payable for `INVOICE_EXPIRY_S` (daemon/src/order_intake.rs:40) — ONE
HOUR. Withdraw does not touch those. A Buyer who pays inside that window is captured and provisioned
normally, on the recipe the operator just declared bad.

So an operator who withdrew because of an incident, an exhausted host, or a broken recipe can still
be handed a paid order up to an hour later, having been told the stop was immediate.

## Why this may be RIGHT, and why it still needs a decision
There is a good argument for the current behaviour: the order was accepted before the stop, the
Buyer paid in good faith against a quote lnrent honoured, and voiding it would refund them net of
fees (ADR-0019) for something they did nothing wrong in. "The money path is the safety mechanism,
not the listing" is this bead's own design principle, and it points at leaving the window alone.

What is NOT acceptable is that the operator is not told. The stop verb is reached for during
incidents, and "immediately" is exactly the word that stops someone looking further.

## What to do — pick ONE and record the reasoning
(a) DISCLOSE ONLY (smallest, probably right): go-live.md states the window explicitly — withdraw
    stops new orders at once, and orders already placed remain payable for up to their invoice
    expiry (1h), so an incident stop should be followed by watching `lnrent subs` / `lnrent status`
    for late settlements. Record in the module docs that this is deliberate.
(b) DISCLOSE + an explicit opt-in: an `--void-pending` flag that also expires OPEN order invoices
    for unprovisioned PENDING subs, so a genuine emergency stop can be total. It must stay opt-in:
    the default must not silently refund Buyers who did nothing wrong.

Do NOT change the default silently in either direction.

## Non-goals
- Do NOT touch capture, refunds, or the reconcile expiry path.
- Do NOT make withdraw cancel PAID-but-unprovisioned orders — that is a refund decision, not a
  publication one.

## Acceptance Criteria
- go-live.md's Stopping section states the in-flight window in plain terms and says what the
  operator should watch after an incident stop.
- The chosen option is recorded with its reasoning where the next reader will find it
  (`daemon/src/listing.rs`'s withdraw docs), so the default is not re-litigated by accident.
- If (b): the flag is opt-in, expires only OPEN invoices of unprovisioned PENDING subs, and is
  tested — including that the default leaves them payable.

title: The phoenixd operator runbook has no owner — u43/ohd/ehu each own a fragment, tof owns none of it
description:
Found by the 2026-07-29 codex+fable status analysis: a seam BETWEEN the phoenixd beads, which each
look complete on their own.

## The gap
The phoenixd work is well covered in pieces and uncovered as a whole:
- lnrent-u43 owns the backup/restore section (seed.dat vs phoenix.conf).
- lnrent-ohd owns economics and onboarding (the first-receive haircut, refund experience, liquidity).
- lnrent-ehu owns the final config-matrix documentation pass.
- lnrent-kr1 ships the `lnrent phoenixd-seed` helper.

NOBODY owns the runbook itself: install phoenixd, point lnrent at it, manage the api password
lifecycle, run phoenixd under a supervisor, use the seed helper, and recover. The fedimint path has
exactly this in docs/go-live.md §§0-7; phoenixd has a warning paragraph (go-live.md:11-24) saying it
is not a supported go-live option, plus fragments spread across four beads.

lnrent-u43's own text says "the phoenixd runbook lnrent-tof will replace it with" — but tof's
acceptance contains NO runbook deliverable. It is a live-money acceptance matrix. So the sentence
points at a bead that does not own the thing.

lnrent-ehu is the backstop, but a backstop that only fires at the FINAL gate is how lnrent-a2b
happened: docs asserting things that stopped being true, discovered late.

## Why it matters more than a docs chore
CONTEXT.md's thesis is an ecosystem of third-party operators, so the runbook IS the product surface
for anyone running phoenixd. It also has a specific practical use: tof is the evidence run, and the
fedimint runbook was proven by being EXECUTED during its acceptance. A phoenixd runbook that exists
before tof can be executed by tof, which is how it gets proven rather than asserted.

## What to build
A phoenixd operator runbook that mirrors the fedimint one's shape, covering at minimum:
- installing and running phoenixd itself (it is an EXTERNAL service lnrent does not manage), under a
  supervisor, and what its data dir contains.
- the `[phoenixd]` config lnrent needs, and the `accept_unsupported` opt-in (lnrent-9gi) with what
  accepting it means.
- deriving the wallet seed with `lnrent phoenixd-seed` (lnrent-kr1).
- the API PASSWORD LIFECYCLE — where it lives, that it regenerates when phoenix.conf is lost, and
  what to do after a restore (lnrent-u43).
- backup obligations: seed.dat restores MONEY, phoenix.conf restores ACCESS, and `lnrentd backup`
  covers neither (it holds lnrent's own correlation index only).
- what `lnrent preflight`'s phoenixd probe reports and each remedy (lnrent-5mi).

## Sequencing
Write it BEFORE tof so tof executes it; fold the measured figures in after (that ordering is already
ohd's, and this bead should not duplicate ohd's economics content — link it).

## Non-goals
- Do NOT advertise phoenixd as go-live approved: that is lnrent-tof's gate and lnrent-ehu's call.
- Do NOT duplicate lnrent-ohd (economics) or lnrent-u43 (the backup/restore facts) — reference them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A phoenixd operator runbook exists with the sections above, in the shape of the fedimint one.
- lnrent-u43's "the runbook tof will replace it with" pointer resolves to this bead instead.
- lnrent-tof's acceptance run EXECUTES it and records where it was wrong or missing.

title: PHASE 1 dogfood: do-vps lifecycle on fedimint — several concurrent subs through renew, expire, suspend, destroy
description:
## Outcome
The author runs the do-vps service on a real DigitalOcean account against the LIVE mainnet fedimint
backend, with SEVERAL concurrent subscriptions carried through DIVERGENT fates — some kept running,
some cancelled early, some renewed, some left to expire — and records what actually happened.

This is PHASE 1 of the operator's own phased programme (dogfood first, public alpha much later):
1. do-vps lifecycle on fedimint  <- THIS BEAD
2. the same on phoenixd (lnrent-tof gates it)
3. a second service (VPN / the existing `recipes/wireguard`)
4. a third service (nostr relay)
5. the same with hardened machines / OS
6. the same with more advanced service configurations
Phases 3-6 are deliberately unfiled: too far out to specify usefully.

## Why this is not already covered
lnrent-7qc CLOSED 2026-07-21 having proven the lnv2 full-daemon path live on mainnet — but it was
ONE order: golden path with teardown, two failed-provision refunds, restart recovery, one sweep.
Every TIME-DRIVEN transition is still unexercised live. The reconcile due-scan arms
(daemon/src/reconcile.rs) that have never run against real money on real droplets:
- `fire_soft_reminder` — mints the renewal invoice and DMs `billing.invoice`
- the renewal PAYMENT + capture extending `paid_through`
- `fire_suspend` — the paid period ran out
- `fire_destroy` — retention elapsed, the droplet is torn down
- `fire_pending_expiry` — an order that was never paid
- `apply_restart_downtime_credit` — the suspend FLOOR after a daemon restart

Those are the paths a real Buyer meets on day 30, not day 0, and they are where the money either
keeps working or quietly stops.

## Deliberately SINGLE-RECIPE
Phase 1 runs ONE recipe (do-vps) with several subscriptions under it. Multi-recipe fleets are
phase 3+, and lnrent-6id (the soft-date reminder mints a renewal at the SERVED recipe's price, not
the subscription's) is that phase's entry condition — it cannot fire here, and fixing it is not a
blocker for this run.

## What to exercise
- Several concurrent subscriptions on one recipe, with different fates: at least one renewed
  (through `fire_soft_reminder` -> invoice -> pay -> capture -> `paid_through` advanced), one
  cancelled by the Buyer and allowed to run out its paid period, one left UNPAID to hit
  `fire_pending_expiry`, and one carried to suspend and then destroy.
- At least one daemon restart mid-run, so `apply_restart_downtime_credit` sizes a real gap.
- The publication gate shipped in lnrent-i23: start quiet, `lnrent listing publish` deliberately,
  and exercise `lnrent listing withdraw` (and a relist) at least once — this is its first live use.
- `lnrent money`, `lnrent subs`, `lnrent teardowns`, `lnrent relays` read as an operator would, and
  operator alert DMs actually arriving.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A recorded run: every command, every state transition observed, and the ledger/DO state at the end.
- Each of the six reconcile arms above is either observed firing or explicitly noted as not reached,
  with the reason.
- Wallet, seed location and closing balance recorded per lnrent-rwv, so this dogfood does not become
  another untracked residual.
- Anything the docs got wrong, or any operator surface that misled, is filed as its own bead.
- Time-compressed periods are acceptable (a short `[pricing] period`) as long as the run states what
  was compressed and what that does NOT prove.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
DECIDED 2026-07-29 (design interview): phase 1 runs on COMPRESSED periods only. The goal is to prove
the state machine in a day, not to watch a real month.

## The floor, and why it is not arbitrary
`pricing.period` is NOT VALIDATED anywhere — `daemon/src/recipe.rs` takes it as a `String` and
`Recipe::validate` checks the service id, hooks, params and operations but none of the timers. So a
compressed recipe can be set to anything and the daemon will accept it, including values that make
the run meaningless.

The binding constraint is that the ORDER INVOICE lives `INVOICE_EXPIRY_S = 3600` — one hour,
hardcoded and deliberately not an operator knob (daemon/src/order_intake.rs:40). Compress `period`
below that and an order's invoice can outlive the very period it pays for: transitions would fire
against a subscription whose invoice is still payable, and nothing observed would generalise to the
30-day case.

So: compress to HOURS, not minutes. A period of ~2-4h with `renew_lead` and `retention` scaled in
proportion keeps every deadline clear of the invoice horizon and still fits the whole lifecycle into
one day. Record the exact values used.

## What a compressed run does NOT prove — state this in the write-up
- that a droplet survives 30 days, or that DigitalOcean bills what was expected over a real month
- that the daemon runs uninterrupted for a month
- that an alert fired at 03:00 actually reaches a human who acts on it
- anything about clock drift, log growth or disk pressure over real time

Those are real and are deliberately NOT phase 1's job. They belong to whatever real-cadence
observation happens later; do not let the compressed run's success be read as covering them.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
DECIDED 2026-07-29 (design interview): phase 1 runs a FRESH WALLET on the EXISTING solomint.

## Why this shape
The federation is a known-good dependency — live mainnet solomint at api.solo.f.blindguardian.net
(verified reachable 2026-07-29: HTTP 405 to a bare GET, which is the expected answer from that API,
in 2.5s), with the ostracoda gateway already vetted through preflight in lnrent-7qc. Re-proving the
join path buys nothing for a lifecycle test, and proving it from scratch is lnrent-2em's job, which
is deliberately deprioritised.

A FRESH wallet, though, matters more here than usual. Phase 1 is the first run whose whole point is
reconciling money at the END — several subscriptions, some refunded, some renewed, a sweep — and a
pre-existing balance with untracked history makes that arithmetic unverifiable. Starting from a
known zero (or a known funded amount) is what makes the closing reconciliation mean anything.

It also satisfies lnrent-rwv BY CONSTRUCTION rather than retrofit: record the seed, its location and
the opening balance on day one, not after the fact.

## BLOCKER found while checking this — the federation invite is not durably recorded
`lnrentd bootstrap` needs `LNRENT_FEDIMINT_INVITE=fed1…`. That invite lived in
/tmp/solomint-invite.txt, which is gone. ~/p/wallets/lnrent-live/README.txt records the two residual
wallets' root secrets and balances but NOT the invite, and no persisted lnrent config survives in
those data dirs. So phase 1 currently cannot bootstrap without going back to the solomint deployment
to re-derive it.

Recoverable — but it stops the run at step one if discovered live, and it is precisely the
recurrence lnrent-rwv exists to stop: the previous dogfood recorded half the wallet material, and
the missing half only surfaced when someone tried to reuse it.

FIRST ACTION for this bead: recover the invite from the solomint deployment and record it durably
alongside the wallet material, then treat "invite recorded" as part of rwv's checklist for every
future dogfood.

## Existing residuals — do not silently absorb them
~/p/wallets/lnrent-live holds lnv2-live (~28 sat) and lnv2-fail (~48 sat) from the 2026-07-20
lnv2_live.rs run. They are NOT part of phase 1's wallet and must not be swept into its arithmetic;
consolidating them is lnrent-rwv's job.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
DECIDED 2026-07-29 (design interview): phase 1 is driven BY HAND; a script is EXTRACTED afterwards
from what was actually done, for phase 2 (lnrent-vam) to reuse.

## Why hand-driven
The transitions are TIME-driven — reconcile fires renew/suspend/destroy on its own — so a Buyer only
acts at order, pay, and optionally renew or cancel. Across ~5 subscriptions that is roughly a dozen
`lnrent-buyer` invocations spread over an afternoon, not a grind.

Writing the harness first would optimise for repetition not yet established, and a script watching a
compressed clock is its own source of bugs. More importantly, a scripted run HIDES the
operator-surface friction this dogfood exists to find: reading `lnrent money`, noticing an alert DM,
working out from `lnrent subs` which subscription is about to suspend. Feeling that is half the point.

## Mechanics that already work (verified)
`lnrent-buyer` takes `--key-file` (or `LNRENT_BUYER_KEY_FILE`) as a GLOBAL arg and `identity new`
generates one, so several buyers are several key files against one binary. The verbs cover the whole
lifecycle: `order`, `renew`, `cancel`, `subs`, `status`, `delivery`, `ops`.

Buyer identity is NOSTR; payment is LIGHTNING. So several buyer identities can all be paid from the
one existing lnd node — no per-buyer wallet needed.

Note `scripts/` holds only `live-fed-e2e.sh`; the "3-seller/5-buyer marketplace sim" referenced in
lnrent-7qc's notes was lnv1-era and is not in the tree. There is no multi-buyer harness to reuse.

## Prepare before starting
A scratch note listing each buyer's key-file path and the FATE it is assigned (renew / cancel /
leave-unpaid / carry-to-destroy). Mid-run, with compressed deadlines arriving, "which sub was
supposed to expire" is exactly what gets lost.

## Afterwards
Extract a driver script from the commands actually run, so lnrent-vam reruns the same lifecycle on
phoenixd instead of re-deriving it. Extraction is cheap once the sequence is known; guessing it up
front is not.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
COMPRESSION INTERACTION found 2026-07-29 while settling the compressed-period decision. Not a
blocker; a value choice to make deliberately before the run.

## The interaction
lnrent-5t3 (open, P3) is that lnrent stamps an lnv2 invoice's `expires_at` AFTER the gateway
round-trip while the fedimint contract deadline was fixed BEFORE it, so the stored value overshoots
the true contract expiry by roughly that fetch. In the drift window a provider-expired row is locally
OPEN and gets reused by create-once.

Against an ORDER invoice that drift is irrelevant: `INVOICE_EXPIRY_S = 3600` is hardcoded and does
not compress, so seconds of drift are a rounding error.

RENEWAL invoices are different. For a `renew.request` inside the credited resumable window,
daemon/src/order_intake.rs:451 clamps the expiry to what is LEFT of that window:
`invoice_expiry_s = remaining.min(INVOICE_EXPIRY_S)`, floored at
`MIN_RENEWAL_INVOICE_EXPIRY_S = 60`. That window derives from the compressed `retention`. At a 60s
renewal invoice, a multi-second gateway fetch is 5-10% of the whole window rather than a rounding
error — so heavy compression makes 5t3 materially more reachable, on exactly the path where a Buyer
renews a SUSPENDED subscription. This run does exercise suspend.

## What to do
Do NOT compress `retention` as hard as `period`. Keep the resumable window comfortably above a few
minutes so renewal invoices land well clear of the 60s floor — the point of the run is the state
machine, not a race against an already-filed bug.

If a renewal inside the resumable window IS attempted deliberately, treat any weirdness there as a
possible 5t3 sighting and record it against that bead rather than debugging it fresh: it would be the
first live observation of a mechanism so far only verified by reading the pinned fedimint source.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
DECIDED 2026-07-29 (design interview): the daemon runs on a VPS, NOT the dev machine, and the setup
is part of this bead.

## Why not local
The compressed run spans hours during which the daemon must stay connected and keep firing reconcile
ticks. A sleeping laptop silently pauses the very clock under test — and worse,
`apply_restart_downtime_credit` would then dutifully credit a downtime gap that was a closed lid
rather than an outage, corrupting the observation instead of merely delaying it. Network changes and
dropped relay connections add failures that are not the product's, and separating those from real
findings costs more than the droplet does.

## The Control node / Hosting plane split — keep it
ADR-0010 (docs/adr/0010-value-plane-vs-hosting-plane.md) separates the Control node from Hosting
boxes. The daemon goes on its OWN droplet; it must NOT be the box it provisions tenants onto. Phase 1
should not be the run that blurs that line.

## PACKAGING BLOCKER, measured — "scp the binary" is not available
The locally built release binary is NOT portable to a stock droplet, for two independent reasons:
- its requested program interpreter is `/nix/store/57iz36553175g3178pvxjij8z5rcsd4n-glibc-2.42-61/
  lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`, a path that does not exist off this machine, so it cannot even start;
- it requires GLIBC_2.39, which is NEWER than Debian 12 bookworm (2.36). Patching the interpreter
  would not rescue it there.

So the honest options are (a) install Nix on the droplet and build there, per go-live.md §2's
`nix develop . --command cargo build --release`, or (b) add a static/musl target to the flake (not
currently configured — the devshell offers native x86_64-gnu + wasm32 only), which drags rocksdb and
aws-lc-sys through a musl build.

TAKE (a) for phase 1. It is the path go-live.md actually documents, so the run exercises what an
operator would really do — and how painful the first build is becomes direct, measured evidence for
lnrent-ea1's priority, obtained without needing lnrent-2em. Record the wall-clock time and the
droplet size it needed; a first rocksdb build is not small.

## Setup outline (Control node)
1. A DO droplet, Debian 12 or Ubuntu 24.04, sized for a Rust+rocksdb build (expect this to dominate
   the size choice, not the daemon's steady-state footprint). SSH key only.
2. Install Nix (Determinate installer), clone the repo, `nix develop . --command cargo build --release
   -p lnrentd -p lnrent-buyer-cli`.
3. Bootstrap per go-live.md §3 with the FRESH wallet decided above, supplying
   `LNRENT_FEDIMINT_INVITE` (recover it first — see the invite gap recorded on this bead) and the
   compressed-period recipe.
4. Deliver the seed by systemd credential or stdin, NOT the run environment — go-live.md §3 forbids
   the env form, and lnrent-y4m.7 clears hook environments to enforce it.
5. Run under systemd with `Restart=always` per go-live.md §6, so the mid-run restart exercises
   `apply_restart_downtime_credit` deliberately rather than by accident.
6. Set `LNRENT_ALERT_NPUB` to a Nostr identity actually read on a phone — the run is supposed to test
   whether alerts REACH a human, and self-DMing the operator key does not.
7. Keep `DO_TOKEN` on the run invocation for provisioning; the tenant droplets it creates are the
   Hosting plane and stay separate from this box.

## What this setup additionally proves
That go-live.md §§2-4 are executable start to finish by someone following them — a cheap partial
rehearsal of lnrent-2em, from the author rather than a stranger, and therefore NOT a substitute for
it. Anything the runbook gets wrong here gets filed, which is the same yield 2em is meant to produce.

comments.author: master
comments.text:
DECIDED 2026-07-29 (design interview): severity-based. Money-safety STOPS the run; everything else is
filed and worked around. Written down now precisely because mid-run — sats moving, droplets billing —
"should I stop?" is a bad question to answer under pressure.

## STOP THE RUN IMMEDIATELY if any of these is observed
These are the invariants the whole money core exists to hold. If one breaks, the run has already told
you its most important thing and continuing risks compounding it:
- the same order or renewal is PAID TWICE, or one payment provisions twice
- a refund goes to a destination the Buyer did not supply
- a liability is booked with nothing spendable behind it (an INV-1 overrun, or a holdings-floor
  breach `lnrent money` reports as covered when it is not)
- the ledger and the wallet disagree in a way `reconcile` cannot account for
- a Buyer PAID and the run reaches a state where they get neither service nor a recorded refund
  liability

Before stopping, CAPTURE STATE FIRST — `lnrent money`, `lnrent subs`, `lnrent teardowns`,
`lnrent status`, and the daemon log tail. A stop that destroys the evidence wastes the finding.

## RECORD AND PUSH THROUGH for everything else
The late-lifecycle transitions are the expensive ones to reach and the setup cost is already paid, so
do not restart the run for:
- any operator-surface confusion: wrong, missing or misleading text anywhere
- an alert that does NOT arrive — that is a finding, not a reason to stop (it is one of the things
  this run exists to test)
- a documented step that is wrong or out of order
- a transition that fires late but correctly
- anything cosmetic in the CLI

File each as its own bead as it happens, with what you saw, and note in the write-up which later
observations were taken with a workaround in place — a contaminated observation is still useful if
labelled.

## The hard stop is stopping the DAEMON, not withdrawing
`lnrent listing withdraw` is the obvious panic button and it is NOT a hard stop: per lnrent-02t it
does not void orders already committed, whose invoices stay payable for up to `INVOICE_EXPIRY_S`
(1h). A Buyer can pay you for the next hour after you "stopped". If you need everything to stop,
stop the systemd unit.

And note what stopping does NOT do: the tenant droplets keep running and keep BILLING. If the run is
aborted rather than finished, tear them down by hand (or via `lnrent teardowns` once the daemon is
back) — do not leave the Hosting plane running against an abandoned Control node.
